name: shopify-app-store-scraper
title: Shopify App Store Scraper: Apps, Ratings and Pricing
description: Get apps from Shopify App Store category lists: name, rating, review count, pricing text, Built for Shopify badge, short description and icon. Optional app page details: developer, launch date, languages and pricing plans.
readme:
# Shopify App Store Scraper

Get the apps listed in Shopify App Store categories as structured data. For each app you get the name, link, rating, review count, pricing text, Built for Shopify badge, short description, icon and its position on the list. Turn on app page details to add the developer, website, launch date, languages, works-with list, categories, pricing plans, highlights and more.

No Shopify account or login is needed. The actor reads public pages on apps.shopify.com.

## What you can do with it

- Track which apps rank in a category and how their ratings and review counts change over time.
- Compare pricing text and pricing plans across competing apps.
- Build a list of app developers with their websites for market research.
- Check which apps carry the Built for Shopify badge.

## Input

| Field | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `startUrls` | list of text | Category list page addresses. Add `?page=2` to start at a later page. |
| `categories` | list of text | Category slugs, the part of the address after `/categories/`. The full list of slugs is in the field description in the input form. |
| `maxResults` | number | Most apps to return in total, read in the order given. Default 50. |
| `maxPages` | number | Most list pages to read per category, about 24 apps per page. Default 5. |
| `includeDetails` | true or false | Open each app page and add the detail fields. Default false. |

If you give no `startUrls` and no `categories` (an empty input), the run reads one popular category (`store-design-site-optimization-seo/all`) and returns at most 20 apps, so a first test run is quick and cheap. Otherwise add at least one entry in `startUrls` or `categories`. Slugs must be real: a guessed slug such as `store-design/all` leads to a "page does not exist" answer. Some slugs end in `/all` (paged lists of about 24 apps), others are overview pages with several sections and no paging, for example `store-design`.

Search addresses (with `q=`), sign-in addresses and the paths `/internal/`, `/services/` and `/login/` are refused. The run stops with a message before any page is read and nothing is charged.

### Example: two categories, two pages each

```json
{
  "categories": [
    "marketing-and-conversion-social-trust-product-reviews/all",
    "store-design-site-optimization-seo/all"
  ],
  "maxResults": 60,
  "maxPages": 2
}
```

### Example: one category with app page details

```json
{
  "startUrls": ["https://apps.shopify.com/categories/marketing-and-conversion-social-trust-product-reviews/all"],
  "maxResults": 5,
  "includeDetails": true
}
```

## Output

Each row is one app. A sample row from a category list:

```json
{
  "handle": "rivyo-product-review",
  "url": "https://apps.shopify.com/rivyo-product-review",
  "name": "Rivyo ‑ Product Reviews App",
  "developer_name": null,
  "rating": 4.9,
  "review_count": 937,
  "pricing_text": "Free to install",
  "built_for_shopify": true,
  "short_description": "Collect unlimited product reviews & build customer loyalty.",
  "icon_url": "https://cdn.shopify.com/app-store/listing_images/.../icon/....png",
  "category": "marketing-and-conversion-social-trust-product-reviews/all",
  "position": 1,
  "page": 2,
  "details_loaded": false
}
```

With `includeDetails` the detail fields are filled, for example `developer_name`, `developer_website`, `developer_address`, `launched_date`, `languages`, `works_with`, `categories`, `pricing_plans`, `highlights`, `rating_counts`, `screenshots` and `similar_apps`. Without it these fields are null. Numbers are numbers, and a value the page does not show is null.

## Pricing

You pay per app returned, plus a small fee when a run starts and delivers its first rows.

| Event | Price |
|---|---|
| Actor start (`actor-start`) | $0.001 |
| App scraped (`app-result`) | $0.0025 |

That is $2.50 per 1,000 apps.

An app that appears in more than one of your categories is returned once. Rows are charged only after they were saved to the dataset. If you set a maximum cost per run, the actor stops when the next app would go over it.

## Limitations

- The list pages do not show the developer. `developer_name` and `developer_url` are null unless `includeDetails` is true.
- Overview pages such as `store-design` show one page of apps grouped in sections, with no further pages.
- Some list sections do not show a short description, so `short_description` can be null.
- App page details cost one extra page read per app, so a run with `includeDetails` takes longer. Rows whose app page could not be read keep their list fields and have `details_loaded` set to false; they are still charged as one app.
- The support email and support link are filled only when the app page shows them. Most pages only say who provides support.
- Customer reviews are not returned, only the rating, the review count, the count per star level and the review summary when the page shows one.
- The App Store changes its layout from time to time. If a page cannot be read, the run says so in its status message.

## FAQ

**Which slugs can I use?**
The input form lists slugs that were loaded and checked. More slugs appear in the links on the App Store home page and on category pages.

**Why did my run stop before maxResults?**
The category had fewer apps, `maxPages` was reached, or the maximum cost per run was hit. The final status message says which.

**Does it need a Shopify login?**
No. Only public pages are read.

**Can I search for apps by keyword?**
No. Search pages are not read. Use category lists instead.

**What happens if the run is restarted by the platform?**
Progress is saved after every batch. A restarted run continues where it stopped and does not return or charge the same apps twice.
